narrative: Material PL1__M9B56DBE shows moderate, fully continuous demand (CV=0.36) across 221 working days with no statistically significant trend. Lead times average 5.53 days with moderate variability (CV=0.26), making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy appropriate. Safety stock of 13,315 units is set at the 95th service level using combined demand-lead time sigma. The EOQ of 31,203 units was capped to 10,361 to respect the 50,800-unit storage constraint, increasing order frequency but maintaining feasibility.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: unconstrained EOQ (31203) reduced to 10361 to satisfy SS+Q <= 50800
Max inventory level (23676) = 50800 * 46.6% — storage is tight; expansion recommended
4 demand outliers detected and winsorised at 1st/99th percentile

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous (100% non-zero days), moderate CV (0.36), and lead times are moderately stable. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is optimal: it minimises total ordering + holding cost via EOQ while the reorder point provides the required 95% service level buffer against demand and lead-time variability.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (50,800 units) is binding: EOQ was reduced from 31,203 to 10,361 units, raising annual orders from ~39 to ~119 and increasing ordering cost. If storage could be expanded to ~45,000 units of usable space above safety stock, the unconstrained EOQ would apply and save an additional ~$9,000/year in ordering costs.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (1016) + safety_stock (13315) = 14331 < max_storage_units (50800); no MOQ-capacity infeasibility
